newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH PAPER UNION SEES THREAT FROM EURO TREND.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH PAPER UNION SEES THREAT FROM EURO TREND.

text.p: The Finnish paper workers' union believes that the exchange rate of the coming single euro currency might move against the U.S. dollar in a way that would not be in the interest of the Finnish economy.
Union chairman Jarmo Lahteenmaki told a seminar on Monday that the European economic and monetary union environment might lead to sharper cyclical fluctuations in the forest industry.
"From Finland's point of view the direction of the floating euro may be wrong," Lahteenmaki said, adding the trend of the Finnish economy would not affect the external value of the euro.
"The single currency would aggravate the cyclical fluctuations of our forest industry in competition with dollar-countries," he said.
"If Sweden remains outside the single currency the situation is very bad for us because Sweden will retain the possibility to conduct an independent exchange rate policy," Lahteenmaki said.

Speaking at an EMU seminar arranged by the Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions (SAK) -- of which the paper workers' union is one of the most influential members -- Lahteenmaki did not voice an opinion for or against Finnish membership of EMU. --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, e-mail news@reuters.fi
